title.en: The Asia-Pacific war and its end
A surprise at dawn in Hawaii

text.en: On a quiet morning in December 1941, American ships lay at anchor in Hawaii. Japan struck without warning, and the war in Asia and the war in Europe suddenly became one.

Japan dreamed of a glorious empire in the same way as Hitler, and it invaded Manchuria in 1931 even though China appealed to the League of Nations.
In 1937 Japan invaded China, seized Beijing and the Shanghai region, and captured the capital Nanjing at the end of the year, where civilians were killed in huge numbers.
Guangzhou and many other places were overrun, and the Chinese army under Chiang Kai-shek retreated to the hills in the west and kept on fighting.
In December 1941 Japan attacked American naval bases at Pearl Harbour in Hawaii without warning, hoping to cripple the Pacific fleet so that it could advance into Southeast Asia unopposed.
Many battleships and fighter planes were destroyed, the United States declared war on Japan, and Britain and China joined in.
This joined the Asia Pacific war and the European war into one cause and brought the United States, with its huge resources, into the Allies.
Japan then swept through Southeast Asia, where Guam, the Philippines, Hong Kong, Singapore, Malaya, the Dutch East Indies, now Indonesia, and Burma fell.
In 1942 the American navy defeated the Japanese navy in the Battle of Midway, which turned the tide in favour of the Allies.
The Battle of Guadalcanal in the Solomon Islands was a joint army and navy offensive lasting several months, and it was another crushing defeat for Japan.
The Americans retook the Philippines, and the Japanese were gradually thrown out of most of their conquests.
In 1944 British and Indian armies pushed back the Japanese who tried to invade north-east India, and together with the Chinese they drove them out of Burma and freed Malaya and Singapore.
The United States built an atomic bomb in a top secret project using the latest science, far more powerful than ordinary explosives.
Japan's generals refused to surrender, so the United States dropped an atomic bomb on Hiroshima, and when they still refused, another on Nagasaki in August 1945.
Japan announced its surrender on 15 August 1945 and signed it formally on 2 September 1945, ending World War II.
The war split the world into two blocs, one led by the United States against Communism and the other by Soviet Russia, and Europe was divided into Communist and non-Communist parts.
The United States and the Soviet Union raced to build nuclear weapons, and defence spending in many countries shot up.
Colonial powers were forced to free their colonies in decolonization, and India was the first to become independent.

problem.en: Why was Pearl Harbour such a turning point of the war?

text.en: Japan attacked American naval bases in Hawaii in December 1941 without warning.

why.en: It wanted to cripple the Pacific fleet before attacking Southeast Asia.

text.en: The United States declared war on Japan, and Britain and China joined.

why.en: The Asia Pacific and European wars became one.

text.en: The United States, with huge resources, joined the Allies.

why.en: This shifted the balance towards the Allies.

prompt.en: Describe how the war in Asia ended.

requiredIdeas.en: Hiroshima and Nagasaki were bombed in August 1945
Japan announced surrender on 15 August and signed on 2 September 1945

commonMisconceptions.en: Saying Japan signed the surrender on 15 August
Thinking Britain dropped the atom bomb

points.en: Pearl Harbour brought the US in; Midway turned the tide.
Hiroshima and Nagasaki; surrender signed on 2 September 1945.
Result: two blocs, nuclear race, decolonization.
